definition.text: A key signature records the sharps or flats that normally apply in a passage, reducing the need to repeat accidentals on individual notes.

anchor.quote: enable the composer to write without using excessive accidentals

facts.text: Correct notation repeats the key signature on every staff and every system.

anchor.quote: writing in the key signature on every staff and every system

facts.text: A temporary modulation can be notated with accidentals rather than a new key signature.

anchor.quote: temporary modulations to other key regions will simply add appropriate accidentals

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 22, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing

definition.text: Major and natural minor scales are distinguished by their ordered patterns of whole steps and half steps between adjacent scale degrees.

anchor.quote: The distinguishing factors of any scale are dependent upon the intervals between each of its steps.

facts.text: The major-scale step pattern is whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.

anchor.quote: whole-step, whole-step, half-step, whole-step, whole-step, whole-step, half-step

facts.text: Natural minor has a whole step from its seventh degree to the tonic, so that degree is called the subtonic.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Key Systems and Terminology
anchor.quote: it is called a subtonic (rather than leading tone)

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 25, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing

definition.text: The minor key system has natural, harmonic, and melodic variants that differ through alterations to the sixth and seventh scale degrees.

anchor.quote: The minor key system has three variants: a) Natural, b) Harmonic, and c) Melodic.

facts.text: Harmonic minor raises the seventh scale degree so it can function as a leading tone.

anchor.quote: The harmonic minor scale includes a raised seventh scale degree

facts.text: Melodic minor raises both the sixth and seventh scale degrees.

anchor.quote: The melodic minor scale includes a raised sixth as well as seventh scale degree.

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 25, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing

definition.text: A written interval is identified by its diatonic span and semitone distance, which together determine labels such as major, minor, augmented, or diminished.

anchor.quote: Intervals were assigned labels based on the scale from which they arose.

facts.text: Four semitones form a major third, while three semitones form a minor third when each spans three scale steps.

anchor.quote: four diatonic half-steps is referred to as a major third, while that of three half-steps is a minor third

facts.text: A tritone can be spelled as an augmented fourth or diminished fifth, and the spelling can imply different resolutions.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Other Interval Names
anchor.quote: their specific spellings can indicate different contexts and possible resolutions

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 25, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing

definition.text: Functional harmony classifies chords by the role they play in a progression, especially tonic, dominant, and pre-dominant functions.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Chord Functions
anchor.quote: hierarchical tonal structures, known as functional harmony, evolved

facts.text: The tonic is built on scale degree one, while pre-dominants are built on degrees two, three, four, and six.

anchor.quote: The tonic is built from the first scale degree and the pre-dominants on the second, third, fourth, and sixth.

facts.text: In minor, raising the third of the fifth-degree chord makes it major and strengthens its dominant function.

anchor.quote: by raising the third of the chord

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 25, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing

definition.text: A seventh chord adds a seventh above a triad, and its function depends on its scale degree and its pull within a tonal progression.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Seventh Chords
anchor.quote: any triad can have a seventh added

facts.text: The supertonic seventh chord functions as a terminal pre-dominant with a strong pull toward the dominant.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Seventh Chords
anchor.quote: the ii7 functions as a terminal pre-dominant chord

facts.text: Adding a seventh to the dominant increases the chord's pull toward the tonic.

anchor.loc: 25 Common Practice Era Scales, Seventh Chords
anchor.quote: increases the force of the chord towards the tonic

attribution: Justin Rubin, Music Composition & Theory (2024), chapter 25, University of Minnesota Libraries Publishing
